methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $13M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Sarla Aviation is a Series A transportation company founded by Rakesh Gaonkar and Adrian Schmidt. The company has raised $13M to date. The broader transportation sector includes eight private peers—among them Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero—and no public comparables, limiting direct peer benchmarking.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using the $13M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $26M. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while three same-sector peers exist, none met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparability, and a broad all-sector median would introduce uncontrolled variance.

The triangulation supports a median valuation of $26M, with a range of $22M (low) to $30M (high). This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and the absence of granular peer anchors in Sarla Aviation's specific stage and subsector. The primary uncertainty is whether the 2.0x multiplier accurately reflects market conditions and company-specific progress metrics for this particular transportation vertical. Additional data on comparable Series A closings or subsequent-round pricing in frontier transportation would strengthen conviction in this range.
